knowledge_point.title: Calculating the Gradient Using the Properties of the Gradient

question.:question/problem:
Find the gradient of the product $f(x,y)g(x,y),$ given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & =- x + y,\quad ∇f(x,y)=(-1)\,i+(1)\,j \\ g(x,y) & =3 x - 4 y,\quad ∇g(x,y)=(3)\,i+(-4)\,j\end{aligned}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The gradient of the product of two functions $f(x,y)$ and $g(x,y)$ is given by

$$
∇[fg]=g∇f+f∇g.
$$

Using the product rule, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}∇[f(x,y)g(x,y)] & =g(x,y)∇f(x,y)+f(x,y)∇g(x,y) \\  & =(3 x - 4 y)((-1)\,i+(1)\,j)+(- x + y)((3)\,i+(-4)\,j) \\  & =(3 x - 4 y)(-1)i+(3 x - 4 y)(1)j+(- x + y)(3)i+(- x + y)(-4)j \\  & =(- 3 x + 4 y)i+(3 x - 4 y)j+(- 3 x + 3 y)i+(4 x - 4 y)j \\  & =(- 6 x + 7 y)\,i+(7 x - 8 y)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Find the gradient of the product $f(x,y)g(x,y),$ given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x,y) & =2 x - 2 y,\quad ∇f(x,y)=(2)\,i+(-2)\,j \\ g(x,y) & =- 3 x - y,\quad ∇g(x,y)=(-3)\,i+(-1)\,j\end{aligned}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The gradient of the product of two functions $f(x,y)$ and $g(x,y)$ is given by

$$
∇[fg]=g∇f+f∇g.
$$

Using the product rule, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}∇[f(x,y)g(x,y)] & =g(x,y)∇f(x,y)+f(x,y)∇g(x,y) \\  & =(- 3 x - y)((2)\,i+(-2)\,j)+(2 x - 2 y)((-3)\,i+(-1)\,j) \\  & =(- 3 x - y)(2)i+(- 3 x - y)(-2)j+(2 x - 2 y)(-3)i+(2 x - 2 y)(-1)j \\  & =(- 6 x - 2 y)i+(6 x + 2 y)j+(- 6 x + 6 y)i+(- 2 x + 2 y)j \\  & =(- 12 x + 4 y)\,i+(4 x + 4 y)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: Find the gradient of the product $f(x,y,z)g(x,y,z),$ given that $f(x,y,z)=x^{2} y^{3} z - x y z^{3}$ and $g(x,y,z)=\frac{1}{x y z}.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The gradient of the product of two functions $f(x,y,z)$ and $g(x,y,z)$ is given by

$$
∇[fg]=g∇f+f∇g.
$$

Now, we calculate the partial derivatives of $f(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(x^{2} y^{3} z - x y z^{3})=2 x y^{3} z - y z^{3} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(x^{2} y^{3} z - x y z^{3})=3 x^{2} y^{2} z - x z^{3} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(x^{2} y^{3} z - x y z^{3})=x^{2} y^{3} - 3 x y z^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}i+\frac{∂f}{∂y}j+\frac{∂f}{∂z}k=(2 x y^{3} z - y z^{3})\,i+(3 x^{2} y^{2} z - x z^{3})\,j+(x^{2} y^{3} - 3 x y z^{2})\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the partial derivatives of $g(x,y,z):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(\frac{1}{x y z})=- \frac{1}{x^{2} y z} \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(\frac{1}{x y z})=- \frac{1}{x y^{2} z} \\ \frac{∂g}{∂z} & =\frac{∂}{∂z}(\frac{1}{x y z})=- \frac{1}{x y z^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}∇g(x,y,z) & =\frac{∂g}{∂x}i+\frac{∂g}{∂y}j+\frac{∂g}{∂z}k=(- \frac{1}{x^{2} y z})\,i+(- \frac{1}{x y^{2} z})\,j+(- \frac{1}{x y z^{2}})\,k\end{aligned}
$$

Using the product rule, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}∇[f(x,y,z)g(x,y,z)] & =g(x,y,z)∇f(x,y,z)+f(x,y,z)∇g(x,y,z) \\  & =(\frac{1}{x y z})((2 x y^{3} z - y z^{3})\,i+(3 x^{2} y^{2} z - x z^{3})\,j+(x^{2} y^{3} - 3 x y z^{2})\,k)+(x^{2} y^{3} z - x y z^{3})((- \frac{1}{x^{2} y z})\,i+(- \frac{1}{x y^{2} z})\,j+(- \frac{1}{x y z^{2}})\,k) \\  & =(\frac{1}{x y z})(2 x y^{3} z - y z^{3})i+(\frac{1}{x y z})(3 x^{2} y^{2} z - x z^{3})j+(\frac{1}{x y z})(x^{2} y^{3} - 3 x y z^{2})k+(x^{2} y^{3} z - x y z^{3})(- \frac{1}{x^{2} y z})i+(x^{2} y^{3} z - x y z^{3})(- \frac{1}{x y^{2} z})j+(x^{2} y^{3} z - x y z^{3})(- \frac{1}{x y z^{2}})k \\  & =(2 y^{2} - \frac{z^{2}}{x})i+(3 x y - \frac{z^{2}}{y})j+(\frac{x y^{2}}{z} - 3 z)k+(- y^{2} + \frac{z^{2}}{x})i+(- x y + \frac{z^{2}}{y})j+(- \frac{x y^{2}}{z} + z)k \\  & =(y^{2})\,i+(2 x y)\,j+(- 2 z)\,k\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: What is the gradient of the product $f(x,y)h(x,y)$ if $f(x,y)=(x+1){e}^{(y+4)}$ and $h(x,y)=(y+4){e}^{(x+1)}?$

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: (- \left(x + 1\right) \left(y + 4\right) e^{x + 1} e^{y + 4} + \left(y + 4\right) e^{x + 1} e^{y + 4})\,i+(\left(x + 1\right) \left(y + 4\right) e^{x + 1} e^{y + 4} - \left(x + 1\right) e^{x + 1} e^{y + 4})\,j

question.:question/worked-solution:
The gradient of the product of two functions $f(x,y)$ and $h(x,y)$ is given by:

$$
∇[fh]=f\,∇\,h+h\,∇\,f\,\,
$$

Now, we calculate the partial derivatives of $f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}((x+1){e}^{(y+4)})={e}^{(y+4)} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}((x+1){e}^{(y+4)})=(x+1){e}^{(y+4)}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\text{ }i+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\text{ }j={e}^{(y+4)}\text{ }i+(x+1){e}^{(y+4)}\text{ }j.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the partial derivatives of $h(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂h}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}((y+4){e}^{(x+1)})=(y+4){e}^{(x+1)} \\ \frac{∂h}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}((y+4){e}^{(x+1)})={e}^{(x+1)}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇h(x,y) & =\frac{∂h}{∂x}\text{ }i+\frac{∂h}{∂y}\text{ }j=(y+4){e}^{(x+1)}\text{ }i+{e}^{(x+1)}\text{ }j.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the product rule, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇[f(x,y)h(x,y)] & =(x+1){e}^{(y+4)}((y+4){e}^{(x+1)}\text{ }i+{e}^{(x+1)}\text{ }j)+(y+4){e}^{(x+1)}({e}^{(y+4)}\text{ }i+(x+1){e}^{(y+4)}\text{ }j) \\  & =(x+1)(y+4){e}^{(x+1)+(y+4)}\text{ }i+(x+1){e}^{(x+1)+(y+4)}\text{ }j+(y+4){e}^{(x+1)+(y+4)}\text{ }i+(x+1)(y+4){e}^{(x+1)+(y+4)}\text{ }j \\  & =((x+1)+1)(y+4){e}^{(x+1)+(y+4)}\text{ }i+(x+1)(1+(y+4)){e}^{(x+1)+(y+4)}\text{ }j\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem: What is the gradient of the product $f(x,y)h(x,y)$ if $f(x,y)=(x-3){e}^{(y+4)}$ and $h(x,y)=(y+4){e}^{(x-3)}?$

:answer-field/choices.:answer/value: (- \left(x - 3\right) \left(y + 4\right) e^{x - 3} e^{y + 4} + \left(y + 4\right) e^{x - 3} e^{y + 4})\,i+(\left(x - 3\right) \left(y + 4\right) e^{x - 3} e^{y + 4} - \left(x - 3\right) e^{x - 3} e^{y + 4})\,j

question.:question/worked-solution:
The gradient of the product of two functions $f(x,y)$ and $h(x,y)$ is given by:

$$
∇[fh]=f\,∇\,h+h\,∇\,f\,\,
$$

Now, we calculate the partial derivatives of $f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}((x-3){e}^{(y+4)})={e}^{(y+4)} \\ \frac{∂f}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}((x-3){e}^{(y+4)})=(x-3){e}^{(y+4)}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂f}{∂x}\text{ }i+\frac{∂f}{∂y}\text{ }j={e}^{(y+4)}\text{ }i+(x-3){e}^{(y+4)}\text{ }j.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate the partial derivatives of $h(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂h}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}((y+4){e}^{(x-3)})=(y+4){e}^{(x-3)} \\ \frac{∂h}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}((y+4){e}^{(x-3)})={e}^{(x-3)}\end{aligned}

$$

Finally, using the product rule, we obtain:

$$
\begin{aligned}∇[f(x,y)h(x,y)] & =(x-3){e}^{(y+4)}((y+4){e}^{(x-3)}\text{ }i+{e}^{(x-3)}\text{ }j)+(y+4){e}^{(x-3)}({e}^{(y+4)}\text{ }i+(x-3){e}^{(y+4)}\text{ }j) \\  & =(x-3)(y+4){e}^{(x-3)+(y+4)}\text{ }i+(x-3){e}^{(x-3)+(y+4)}\text{ }j+(y+4){e}^{(x-3)+(y+4)}\text{ }i+(x-3)(y+4){e}^{(x-3)+(y+4)}\text{ }j \\  & =((x-3)+1)(y+4){e}^{(x-3)+(y+4)}\text{ }i+(x-3)(1+(y+4)){e}^{(x-3)+(y+4)}\text{ }j\end{aligned}
